baslik: Europe's Deadliest Mine Disaster — and the Men Who Walked Out 20 Days Later
sonuc: were swept by a coal dust explosion
tetik: an ignition that set off coal dust through connected galleries
mekanizma: coal dust explosion propagating through interconnected workings
ders: France improved mine rescue services and dust suppression
yanilgi: Rescue was called off too early. Survivors emerged on their own weeks after the explosion.
tartisma: Rescuers stopped searching while men were still alive underground. When do you stop a rescue?
basliklar: Why the Courrières Mine Exploded
The Miners Who Walked Out Weeks Later
sahneler: An explosion tore through the Courrières coal mines in northern France.
It swept through the galleries, killing one thousand ninety nine miners.
It was Europe's deadliest mining disaster.
Coal dust in the air turned an ignition into a racing explosion.
The mine's galleries were connected, so the blast spread widely.
Rescue efforts were scaled back within days.
Weeks later, a group of survivors walked out on their own.
France then improved mine rescue and dust control.

baslik: Britain's Worst Mining Disaster Began With a Spark
tetik: methane ignited, probably by sparks from electrical signalling gear
mekanizma: firedamp ignition that set off a coal dust explosion
ders: the mine's owners were prosecuted for safety breaches and mine safety law was enforced more strictly
yanilgi: The mine had exploded before, in 1901. The same hazards were still there twelve years later.
tartisma: The owners were fined a trivial sum. What does a small fine say about the value of safety?
basliklar: Why the Senghenydd Colliery Exploded
The Mine That Exploded Twice
sahneler: A coal mine in the Welsh village of Senghenydd exploded.
Fire and poisonous gas spread through the tunnels, killing four hundred thirty nine miners.
It remains Britain's worst mining disaster.
Methane had built up in the workings.
It was probably ignited by sparks from electrical signalling equipment.
The blast lifted coal dust, which exploded too.
The same mine had exploded twelve years earlier.
Its owners were prosecuted, but fined only a small sum.

baslik: The New Zealand Mine With One Way Out
tetik: a large build-up of methane in the mine
mekanizma: methane explosion in a mine with inadequate gas drainage and a single exit
ders: New Zealand rewrote its workplace health and safety law
yanilgi: The mine wasn't old. It was new and still ramping up production when it exploded.
tartisma: Gas warnings had been logged many times. Why did production continue?
basliklar: Why the Pike River Mine Exploded
The Mine With a Single Exit
sahneler: An explosion ripped through the Pike River coal mine in New Zealand.
Twenty nine men underground were killed.
The mine was new, still ramping up production.
Methane was not being drained well enough.
Gas warnings had been logged again and again.
The mine had only one practical way out.
More explosions followed, making rescue impossible.
New Zealand rewrote its workplace safety law.

baslik: The Mine Fire That Filled the Tunnels With Carbon Monoxide
sonuc: caught fire, filling its tunnels with toxic gas
tetik: an underground fire spreading carbon monoxide
mekanizma: mine fire producing carbon monoxide that spread through the ventilation network
yanilgi: Most miners weren't killed by flames. They were overcome by carbon monoxide carried through the tunnels.
tartisma: Many victims lacked adequate escape equipment. What is the minimum a miner should carry?
basliklar: Why the Soma Mine Disaster Happened
The Gas That Spread Through the Tunnels
sahneler: A fire broke out deep inside a coal mine in Soma, Turkey.
Toxic gas spread through the tunnels, and three hundred one miners died.
Most weren't killed by flames.
The fire produced carbon monoxide.
The ventilation system carried it through the mine.
Many miners couldn't reach safety in time.
It was the deadliest mining disaster in Turkey's history.
Mining safety rules were tightened afterward.

baslik: The Underground Fire That Has Burned for Decades
tetik: a fire in a landfill spreading into abandoned coal workings
mekanizma: a coal seam fire fed by air through old mine tunnels
ders: the town was largely abandoned through a federal buyout
yanilgi: The fire isn't a single blaze. It creeps slowly through coal seams, fed by air from old tunnels.
tartisma: Early efforts to put it out were small and underfunded. How much would stopping it early have cost?
basliklar: Why the Centralia Mine Fire Won't Go Out
The Town Abandoned Over a Fire Below
soru: What would stopping it early cost?
sahneler: Under a Pennsylvania town, a coal fire has burned for decades.
Toxic gas spread and the ground collapsed into sinkholes.
It began with a fire at a landfill.
The flames spread into old mine tunnels below.
Those tunnels fed air to the coal seams.
Early attempts to stop it were too small.
Most residents eventually had to leave.
Centralia became a near ghost town above a fire that won't go out.

baslik: Workers Were Sent Back Into a Cracked Building
mekanizma: overloaded structure with illegal floors, heavy machinery and generators on weak ground
ders: factory safety agreements brought independent building inspections to Bangladesh
yanilgi: The cracks were seen the day before. Shops downstairs closed, but garment workers were ordered back in.
tartisma: Global brands sourced clothes from the building. How far does responsibility extend in a supply chain?
basliklar: Why Rana Plaza Collapsed
The Cracks That Were Ignored
sahneler: An eight-storey building near Dhaka collapsed during the morning shift.
It crushed thousands of garment workers, and one thousand one hundred thirty four died.
Cracks had appeared the day before.
Shops on the ground floor closed.
But garment workers were ordered back in.
The building had extra floors added illegally and stood on weak ground.
Heavy generators shook the structure when the power cut out.
Independent factory inspections followed across Bangladesh.

baslik: The Locked Doors That Trapped Garment Workers in a Fire
tetik: a fire in scrap fabric on a crowded factory floor
mekanizma: rapid fire spread with locked exit doors and a fire escape that collapsed
ders: New York passed sweeping fire safety and labor laws
yanilgi: The building itself was considered fireproof. The people inside were not protected.
tartisma: Doors were locked to prevent theft and breaks. How often do rules for control override safety?
basliklar: Why the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire Was So Deadly
The Fireproof Building That Trapped Its Workers
sahneler: Fire swept through a garment factory in New York.
Workers were trapped on the upper floors, and one hundred forty six died.
It started in a bin of scrap fabric.
One exit door was locked.
The fire escape collapsed under the crowd.
Fire ladders couldn't reach the upper floors.
The building itself was called fireproof.
New York then passed sweeping fire safety and labor laws.

baslik: The Factory Wastewater That Poisoned a Fishing Town
sonuc: poisoned people who ate its fish
tetik: methylmercury in a chemical factory's wastewater
mekanizma: bioaccumulation of methylmercury through the marine food chain
ders: the Minamata Convention on Mercury was named after the town
yanilgi: The water didn't poison people directly. Mercury built up through the food chain until fish carried dangerous doses.
tartisma: The cause was suspected years before discharges stopped. How much proof is enough to act?
basliklar: What Caused Minamata Disease
The Mercury That Climbed the Food Chain
sahneler: In a Japanese fishing town, people began to suffer a mysterious disease.
Some were killed, and thousands were left disabled.
Cats in the town were affected first.
A chemical factory was releasing methylmercury into the bay.
Small organisms absorbed it, then fish ate them.
Mercury built up at each step of the food chain.
People who ate the fish received toxic doses.
A global treaty on mercury now bears Minamata's name.

baslik: The School Built on a Chemical Waste Dump
sonuc: leaked buried chemicals into a neighbourhood
tetik: construction breaking the clay cap over buried waste
mekanizma: breach of a chemical waste landfill's cap, letting contaminated water migrate into homes
ders: the US created the Superfund law to clean up hazardous waste sites
zincir: CHEMICAL WASTE BURIED IN A CANAL
SCHOOL AND HOMES BUILT ON TOP
yanilgi: The waste wasn't hidden in secret. It was sold with a deed warning about the chemicals buried there.
tartisma: The land was sold for one dollar with a warning. Who is responsible after the warning?
basliklar: What Went Wrong at Love Canal
The Neighbourhood Built on Buried Chemicals
soru: Who owns the risk after a warning?
sahneler: In Niagara Falls, chemicals began seeping into homes and a school.
Families were evacuated as contamination spread through the neighbourhood.
The area had been a chemical waste dump.
Waste was buried in an old canal and covered with clay.
Later, a school and homes were built on top.
Construction broke the cap, and water carried chemicals out.
It became a national emergency.
The US then created the Superfund law.

baslik: The Mining Dam That Turned to Liquid in Seconds
sonuc: collapsed and buried a mining complex in mud
tetik: saturated tailings losing strength all at once
mekanizma: static liquefaction of an upstream-raised tailings dam
zincir: DAM RAISED UPSTREAM ON ITS OWN WASTE
yanilgi: No heavy rainstorm triggered it. The saturated waste inside the dam suddenly lost its strength.
tartisma: The dam had been certified stable months earlier. What is a stability certificate worth?
basliklar: Why the Brumadinho Dam Collapsed
The Dam That Liquefied in Seconds
sahneler: A mining waste dam in Brazil collapsed in seconds.
A wave of mud buried offices and a cafeteria, and two hundred seventy people were killed.
The dam was built on top of its own waste.
That waste was still saturated with water.
Suddenly, it lost its strength and flowed like liquid.
The dam had been certified stable months before.
It became one of Brazil's worst industrial disasters.
Brazil then banned this type of dam.

baslik: The Mudflow That Travelled Hundreds of Kilometres to the Sea
sonuc: released a mudflow that reached the Atlantic
tetik: liquefaction in an upstream-raised tailings dam
mekanizma: liquefaction of saturated tailings in an upstream-construction dam
yanilgi: The damage didn't stop at the village. The mud travelled down the Rio Doce all the way to the ocean.
tartisma: Three years later, a similar dam failed at Brumadinho. Why wasn't the first warning enough?
basliklar: Why the Mariana Dam Collapsed
The Mudflow That Reached the Ocean
sahneler: A mining waste dam near Mariana, Brazil, suddenly burst.
A flood of mud destroyed the village of Bento Rodrigues, and nineteen people were killed.
The mud poured into the Rio Doce.
It travelled down the river all the way to the Atlantic.
The dam had been raised upstream, on top of its own waste.
Saturated tailings inside it liquefied.
Three years later, a similar dam failed at Brumadinho.
Brazil then tightened oversight of tailings dams.

baslik: The Wall That Released a Flood of Caustic Red Mud
sonuc: flooded villages with caustic red mud
tetik: a corner of a waste reservoir wall giving way
mekanizma: structural failure of a reservoir dyke holding highly alkaline bauxite residue
ders: Hungary tightened industrial waste reservoir regulation
yanilgi: The mud wasn't just dirty water. It was strongly alkaline and caused chemical burns.
tartisma: The reservoir had been inspected shortly before. What are inspections actually checking?
basliklar: Why the Ajka Red Mud Reservoir Failed
The Caustic Flood in Hungary
sahneler: A reservoir wall at a Hungarian alumina plant suddenly broke.
A flood of red mud swept through nearby villages, and ten people were killed.
The mud was waste from making aluminium.
It was strongly alkaline.
It caused chemical burns to people and animals.
It flowed into rivers and reached the Danube.
The reservoir had been inspected shortly before.
Hungary then tightened rules for industrial waste reservoirs.

commons: Kingston Fossil Plant coal fly ash slurry spill
baslik: The Coal Ash Pond That Buried a River Valley
sonuc: burst and buried the land around it in coal ash
tetik: a dike built on weak, wet ash failing
mekanizma: failure of a dike founded on a soft layer of wet ash and slimes
ders: the US set national rules for coal ash disposal
yanilgi: The dike didn't fail from a single storm. It was built on top of old, weak ash that couldn't carry it.
tartisma: Workers who cleaned up the spill later reported illnesses. Who protects the cleanup crew?
basliklar: Why the Kingston Coal Ash Dike Failed
The Ash Spill That Buried a Valley
sahneler: At a Tennessee power plant, a coal ash pond burst.
A flood of ash slurry swept over the land, destroying homes.
Ash had been stored wet behind earth dikes.
Over the years, the dikes were raised higher on top of old ash.
Beneath them lay a soft, weak layer.
The dike collapsed, and ash poured into the river valley.
Cleanup took years.
The US then set national rules for coal ash disposal.

baslik: A Hidden Clay Layer Failed Under a Mine Waste Dam
sonuc: breached and released mine waste into lakes
tetik: a weak glacial clay layer beneath the dam
mekanizma: foundation failure through an undetected weak glaciolacustrine clay layer
ders: British Columbia strengthened tailings dam design requirements
yanilgi: The dam wasn't simply overfilled. The ground beneath it held a weak clay layer investigations had missed.
tartisma: The clay layer was thin and easy to miss. How deep should a site investigation go?
basliklar: Why the Mount Polley Dam Failed
The Clay Layer Nobody Found
sahneler: A mine waste dam in British Columbia suddenly breached.
Within hours, water and mine waste rushed into nearby lakes and creeks.
The dam itself wasn't the weak point.
Beneath it lay a thin layer of glacial clay.
Site investigations had not identified how weak it was.
As the dam grew steeper, the clay sheared.
The foundation slid, and the dam opened.
British Columbia strengthened tailings dam requirements.

baslik: The Florida Condo That Collapsed in the Night
sonuc: partially collapsed in the middle of the night
tetik: long-term structural damage around the pool deck
mekanizma: investigations focus on deteriorated concrete and reinforcement at the pool deck and its connections
ders: Florida required regular structural recertification of older condominiums
yanilgi: The damage was not unknown. An engineer's report years earlier warned of major structural damage below the pool deck.
tartisma: Residents were debating the cost of repairs when it fell. Who decides when repairs can't wait?
basliklar: Why the Surfside Condo Collapsed
The Warning Report Years Before
sahneler: In the middle of the night, part of a Florida condo tower collapsed.
Residents were asleep, and ninety eight people were killed.
Investigators focused on the pool deck next to the tower.
Water had damaged the concrete and steel beneath it for years.
An engineer's report years earlier warned of major damage.
Repairs were debated and delayed.
The final investigation into the exact sequence continues.
Florida now requires older condos to be structurally recertified.

baslik: Record Snow Collapsed a Cinema Roof Onto Its Audience
sonuc: had its roof collapse during a film
tetik: heavy wet snow from a record blizzard
mekanizma: roof trusses slipping off their bearings under a heavy snow load
ders: Washington tightened its building codes and inspections
zincir: HEAVY WET SNOW ON FLAT ROOF
yanilgi: The snow alone didn't bring it down. The roof's steel trusses weren't properly anchored to the walls.
tartisma: The architect and builder were later blamed. Should designers be held accountable decades later?
basliklar: Why the Knickerbocker Theatre Roof Collapsed
The Snow That Brought Down a Cinema
sahneler: During a film, the roof of a Washington cinema collapsed.
It crushed the audience below, and ninety eight people were killed.
A record blizzard had buried the city.
Heavy, wet snow piled on the flat roof.
The roof's steel trusses weren't properly anchored to the walls.
They slipped, and the roof dropped onto the balcony.
The balcony and walls came down with it.
Washington tightened its building codes afterward.

baslik: The Tehran Tower That Collapsed During a Fire
sonuc: collapsed while firefighters fought a fire inside
tetik: a long fire heating unprotected steel
mekanizma: fire weakening steel members lacking adequate fire protection
ders: Tehran began reviewing the fire safety of older high-rises
yanilgi: The building didn't collapse instantly. It burned for hours before the weakened steel gave way.
tartisma: The building had received repeated safety warnings. Why do warnings about old buildings go unheeded?
basliklar: Why the Plasco Building Collapsed
The Fire That Brought Down a Tehran Landmark
sahneler: A high-rise landmark in Tehran caught fire.
Hours later, it collapsed, and firefighters inside were killed.
The building was old and packed with goods.
Its steel frame had little fire protection.
As the fire burned, the steel heated and weakened.
Floors gave way, and the tower came down.
The building had received safety warnings before.
Tehran began reviewing the fire safety of older towers.

baslik: The Glued Timber Roof That Collapsed Under Snow
sonuc: had its roof collapse onto skaters
tetik: snow load on glued timber beams weakened for years
mekanizma: failure of glued laminated timber beams degraded by moisture and an unsuitable adhesive
ders: Germany introduced mandatory inspections for large-span public roofs
yanilgi: The snow wasn't extreme for the region. The beams had lost much of their strength long before.
tartisma: The rink was due to close because of the snow. How close is too close to a decision?
basliklar: Why the Bad Reichenhall Ice Rink Roof Collapsed
The Glue That Failed Over Years
sahneler: The roof of an ice rink in Bavaria collapsed onto skaters.
Children were among the fifteen people killed.
The roof rested on glued timber beams.
The adhesive used was unsuitable for the conditions.
Moisture had weakened the joints over many years.
Heavy snow was more than the degraded beams could carry.
The rink was about to be closed because of the snow.
Germany then required inspections of large public roofs.

baslik: How Engineers Stopped the Leaning Tower From Falling
sonuc: was closed because it was leaning toward collapse
tetik: a shallow foundation on soft, uneven soil
mekanizma: differential settlement of a shallow foundation in soft clay
ders: soil extraction under the high side reduced the lean
yanilgi: The lean wasn't a design choice. It began during construction, when one side sank into soft soil.
tartisma: Engineers straightened it only slightly, not fully. Should a flaw that made it famous be preserved?
basliklar: Why the Leaning Tower of Pisa Leans
How Engineers Saved the Leaning Tower
sahneler: The Leaning Tower of Pisa was closed because it was falling over.
Its lean kept growing until collapse became a real risk.
The tilt began during construction.
Its foundation was shallow, and the soil beneath was soft and uneven.
One side sank more than the other.
Engineers carefully removed soil from under the high side.
The tower settled back slightly and stopped moving.
It reopened, still leaning, but stable.
